title: Elemental Alchemy — Chapter 10 developmental doctrine
governing_principle: The protagonist is the foreground. The framework is the map underneath the story.

recognition_principle.name: Elemental recognition follows movement before vocabulary
recognition_principle.statement: An element is recognised by what HAPPENS in a passage, not by whether the passage uses the element's name. A lens that searches only for 'aether' is a concordance; a lens that recognises non-forcing, release of control, and reorganization from a larger field can detect phenomenology before terminology.
recognition_principle.constraint: OBSERVATION ONLY — never automatic classification. A movement match is a reason to read the passage, never a ruling that the passage IS that element.

developmental_thesis: You have now encountered the elements individually. This chapter lets us watch them move together in one life.
position_note: Chapter 10 is the last chapter before the Conclusion. The reader has already walked Fire through Aether in chapters 5-9.
teaching_sequence_note: Experience first -> name second -> brief orientation -> return to experience. A section that defines before it depicts inverts the doctrine.

elements.question: Why
elements.movement: She descends into what hurts and what matters.

elements.question: How
elements.movement: She has to build something real.
The field holding it all. Shown, not described.

narrative_target: When the Old Life No Longer Fits
Giving the New Life a Body
The Still Point in the Turning

prospective_patterns: this first section of the book
editorial_test: Is this helping me experience the spiral through the protagonist, or stopping the story so the spiral can be explained?
success_condition: By the end, the protagonist should barely need the words 'Spiralogic Process'. She should simply be living the spiral.

element_signatures._note: Movement signatures, so a passage can be recognised as elemental by what HAPPENS in it, not by whether it uses the element's name. Aether especially: the doctrine asks for it to be shown, not described, and a shown Aether moment rarely says 'aether'.

doctrine_principles.spiral_recurrence: A passage that carries three or more elements AND returns to an earlier one demonstrates recurrence rather than sequence. This is the hardest thing to teach and the easiest to lose.
